nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $p$ be a multivariate polynomial over $R$ in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, let $i \in \sigma$ and $x : \sigma \to R$, and for a polynomial $q$ write $q_{i,x} \in R[X]$ for its univariate specialization that keeps $X_i$ as the variable $X$ and sets every other $X_j$ to $x_j$. Then $(\partial p / \partial X_i)_{i,x} = (p_{i,x})'$, the derivative of $p_{i,x}$.
nodes.title: Partial derivatives under univariate specialization

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $p$ be a multivariate polynomial over $R$ in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, and let $i \in \sigma$, $x : \sigma \to R$ and $t \in R$. Evaluating at $t$ the univariate specialization of $p$ that keeps $X_i$ as the variable and sets every other $X_j$ to $x_j$ gives $p(y)$, where $y_i = t$ and $y_j = x_j$ for $j \ne i$.
nodes.title: Evaluating a univariate specialization

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a real stable complex multivariate polynomial in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, let $i \in \sigma$, and for $x : \sigma \to \mathbb{C}$ write $p_{i,x} \in \mathbb{C}[X]$ for the univariate specialization of $p$ that keeps $X_i$ as the variable $X$ and sets every other $X_j$ to $x_j$. Suppose there is a natural number $d$ such that for every $x : \sigma \to \mathbb{C}$ the polynomial $p_{i,x}$…
nodes.title: Real-rootedness of univariate specializations of real stable polynomials

nodes.summary: A complex multivariate polynomial is real stable if it is stable and has real coefficients.
nodes.title: Real stable polynomials

nodes.summary: A complex multivariate polynomial is stable if it has no zero when every variable lies in the open upper half-plane.
nodes.title: Stable polynomials

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a complex multivariate polynomial with real coefficients in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, let $i \in \sigma$, and let $a : \sigma \to \mathbb{C}$ with $a_j$ real for every $j \ne i$. Then the univariate specialization of $p$ that keeps $X_i$ as the variable and sets every other $X_j$ to $a_j$ has real coefficients.
nodes.title: Univariate specialization at real values preserves real coefficients

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a real stable complex multivariate polynomial in variables $X_s$ indexed by $s \in \sigma$, and write $\partial_s$ for the partial derivative with respect to $X_s$. For every finite list $(i_1, \dots, i_k)$ of indices in $\sigma$ (repetitions allowed, possibly empty), the mixed differential of $p$ along the list, $(1 - \partial_{i_k}) \cdots (1 - \partial_{i_1})\, p$, is real stable.
nodes.title: The mixed differential preserves real stability

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a stable complex multivariate polynomial in variables $X_s$ indexed by $s \in \sigma$, and write $\partial_s$ for the partial derivative with respect to $X_s$. For every finite list $(i_1, \dots, i_k)$ of indices in $\sigma$ (repetitions allowed, possibly empty), the mixed differential of $p$ along the list, $(1 - \partial_{i_k}) \cdots (1 - \partial_{i_1})\, p$, is stable.
nodes.title: The mixed differential preserves stability

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a stable complex multivariate polynomial in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, let $i \in \sigma$, and let $a : \sigma \to \mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Im} a_j \ge 0$ for every $j \ne i$. If the univariate specialization of $p$ that keeps $X_i$ as the variable and sets every other $X_j$ to $a_j$ is nonzero, then every root $w$ of it satisfies $\operatorname{Im} w \le 0$.
nodes.title: Roots of specializations of stable polynomials lie in the closed lower half-plane

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a real stable complex multivariate polynomial in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, let $i \in \sigma$, and write $\partial_i p$ for the partial derivative of $p$ with respect to $X_i$. Then $p - \partial_i p$ is real stable.
nodes.title: Subtracting a partial derivative preserves real stability

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a stable complex multivariate polynomial in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, let $i \in \sigma$, and write $\partial_i p$ for the partial derivative of $p$ with respect to $X_i$. Then $p - \partial_i p$ is stable.
nodes.title: Subtracting a partial derivative preserves stability

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $p$ be a multivariate polynomial over $R$ in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, and let $i \in \sigma$ and $x : \sigma \to R$. The univariate specialization of $p$ at $i$ and $x$ is the polynomial in $R[X]$ obtained from $p$ by substituting $X$ for $X_i$ and the constant $x_j$ for every $X_j$ with $j \ne i$; the value $x_i$ is not used.
nodes.title: Univariate specialization

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
